title: Transformer-Based Feedback Error Learning in Control System of Servo Motor
content: In the neural network of conventional feedback error learning (FEL), the sigmoid function used as the activation function confines the output to a fixed range; consequently, the learning effect tends to fall into a local minimum even as learning time elapses. Furthermore, since the compensation is determined only from the target trajectory at each time instant without referring to the past control history, it has been difficult to form the compensation quickly in the transient state and to improve the responsiveness of the control. To address these problems, this paper proposed feedback error learning for servo motor using a Transformer. In the proposed method, the conventional neural network was replaced with a Transformer, which directly refers to all time instants in the recent history of the target trajectory through attention, and the output layer was made linear to avoid saturation and improve learning efficiency. Furthermore, a learning scheme that switches the parameters to be learned and the data used for learning when a disturbance is detected from the tracking error was combined so that the compensation adapts quickly after load variations. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, simulations of servo-motor positioning control were performed in Python. In simulations of tracking control of a sinusoidal reference with a load variation applied midway, the proposed method shortened the settling time in the initial learning period by about 53 % and reduced the steady-state error before the load variation by about 85 % compared with the conventional method. It was also confirmed that the maximum error immediately after the load variation was reduced by about 49 %. These results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method.
